claim: Faster generation can increase the importance of explicit intent for controlling what is produced.
status: Participant-argued relationship and analyst synthesis; not a tested causal effect
qualification: Generation volume and useful constraint vary; E245 rejects the assumption that more constraint is always better.

claim: Represented context provides material for scrutiny, while acceptance still depends on how the work is checked and who approves it.
qualification: Knowledge artifacts do not assign accountability or guarantee reliable checking; E203 conditions possible reduced involvement on validated explanations and cheaper checks.

claim: Shorter generation and shifted effort motivate reconsideration of staging, decomposition and coordination.
status: Mixed current work description and prospective process interpretation
qualification: Reported current decomposition and imagined orchestration remain separate; no established universal lifecycle transition.

claim: Redistributing execution or architectural tasks need not redistribute answerability in the same way.
status: Reported divisions plus conditional and future interpretation
qualification: Who takes responsibility varies by team/organization; retained human accountability is not a verified legal allocation or proof of unchanged authority.

claim: Shared delivery arrangements offer ways to coordinate people and agents across individual working contexts.
status: One bounded operational example plus desired/interpretive possibilities
qualification: The feedback practice in E149 does not establish full team-agent orchestration or demonstrate that a shared process changes job boundaries.

claim: Retaining human oversight creates a need to sustain the capacities used to understand and review outputs.
status: Participant-argued dependency, supported by practices; no longitudinal effectiveness test
qualification: Teaching, mentoring and reviews are not proven learning outcomes; E201 envisages alternatives to learning by writing every line.

claim: Shifting work from creation toward review can create tensions over learning, agency and enjoyable work.
status: Interpretive and normative connection with colleague-reported preferences
qualification: E105/E264 provide positive creativity/enjoyment accounts; no inevitable deskilling or morale decline is inferred.

claim: Contextual judgment can inform what people accept and supervise; its attributed value is distinct from the allocation of authority and answerability.
status: Interpretive relationship between contribution and acceptance; not a causal or legal finding
qualification: Shared evidence can illuminate different analytic questions. Accountability does not demonstrate value, and value does not confer authority.

claim: Learning and work arrangements are proposed as ways to sustain the understanding and judgment participants value.
status: Participant-argued and analyst-synthesized dependency; no longitudinal effectiveness test
qualification: Current learning practices, expected expertise and desired pathways remain separate. Learning outcomes and professional value are not independently measured.
